Implemented concurrent SQLite and NATS task dispatch using containers.max_concurrency, with default same-repo serialization and race-tested dispatcher coverage.

Added config.Repo.AllowConcurrent (allow_concurrent toml key) and threaded it through taskDispatcher so opted-in repos skip the default FIFO same-repo serialization while still respecting containers.max_concurrency. Worktrees are already keyed per issue number, so no on-disk collision. Race-tested dispatcher coverage added.

Completed JetStream task dispatch and NATS agent request/reply, including token_env authentication for archied and canonical NATS_URL/NATS_TOKEN propagation to container workers; anonymous local mode remains supported and race-tested.

Added internal/storerpc: core-NATS request/reply RPC so archie-agent can call Store.Update/Transition without direct DB access. archied's Store stays the sole owner; store.Task gained json tags to cross the wire. Not yet wired into daemon.go or workflow.TaskContext — that's archie-core-5zh.4's job once all three RPC proxies exist.

Added internal/forgerpc: core-NATS request/reply RPC for the four forge.Forge methods workflow stages actually call mid-run (Comment, CloseIssue, CreatePR, SetStateLabel). Confirmed via grep that all other Forge methods (AssignedIssues, IssuesWithLabel, React, RepliesAfter, PRState, CreateIssue, AcceptInvitations, VerifyPush) are daemon-only poll/reconcile-loop calls, never invoked from a workflow stage, so nothing else needs proxying. archied stays the sole holder of forge API tokens. Not yet wired into daemon.go or workflow.TaskContext — deferred to archie-core-5zh.4.

Added internal/worktreerpc: core-NATS request/reply RPC so archie-agent can request a git push without holding the forge push token. Server resolves the worktree directory itself from owner/repo/issue (never trusts a path from the sandboxed agent) and calls the daemon's own worktree.Manager.Push, which already holds the token via its askpass helper. Prepare/CommitAll/Diff/ChangedFiles/ChangedLines stay local git ops the agent can run directly against its bind-mounted worktree — only Push needed proxying. Not yet wired into daemon.go or workflow.TaskContext — deferred to archie-core-5zh.4, which now has all three RPC proxies (Store, Forge, worktree push) it depends on.

Superseded by finer-grained sub-issues 5zh.5 (TaskConfig payload), 5zh.6 (TaskContext interface refactor), 5zh.7 (archie-agent full-task handler), 5zh.8 (daemon.go handoff), 5zh.9 (register RPC servers in archied). The original single acceptance criterion (workflow.Route/Run execute in archie-agent) is satisfied once 5zh.7 and 5zh.8 land; splitting further because implementation revealed real design forks (Prepare needing the push token, tc.Cfg needing a curated non-secret payload) that each warrant their own test-first pass.

Implemented curated non-secret TaskConfig/TaskForge payload with detached map snapshots, stable JSON Duration encoding, full Repo JSON tags, and regression coverage. Focused config tests, go vet, go fix -diff, and full race suite pass; repository-wide lint remains blocked only by 36 unrelated pre-existing findings.

Trimmed workflow.TaskContext.Forge/Store/Trees to new interfaces (Forger, TaskStore, Trees) in internal/workflow/workflow.go, scoped to exactly the methods stages call mid-run (4 Forge methods, 2 Store methods, 6 Trees methods). Go's structural typing meant zero changes were needed anywhere else — forge.Forge (already an interface), *store.Store, and *worktree.Manager all satisfy the new interfaces automatically, and storerpc.Client/forgerpc.Client/worktreerpc.Client already match by construction from 5zh.1-3. Full build, race suite, vet, and staticcheck all clean with no behavior change. archie-core-5zh.7 (archie-agent full-task handler) and 5zh.9 (register RPC servers in archied) are now unblocked.

Added registerTaskRPCServers() in cmd/archied/main.go, wiring storerpc.Server/forgerpc.Server/worktreerpc.Server onto the daemon's NATS connection whenever [nats] is configured, alongside the existing worktree.Manager and forge/store instances the daemon already owns. Test spins an embedded NATS server, registers via the composed function, then round-trips real storerpc/forgerpc/worktreerpc clients against it to prove all three are reachable. archie-core-5zh.7 (archie-agent full-task handler) can now be built and tested end-to-end against a real archied.

Added internal/taskrun (Request/Response wire types + SubjectForTask) and cmd/archie-agent/taskrun.go: runTask builds a workflow.Registry from the container's own bind-mounted worktree (skillbuild.BuildRegistry, same call the daemon already makes), routes and runs the task's entire workflow via workflow.Route/workflow.Run, using storerpc.Client/forgerpc.Client for Store/Forge and a new hybridTrees (worktreerpc.Client for Prepare/Push, local *worktree.Manager for CommitAll/Diff/ChangedFiles/ChangedLines against the mount). Added config.TaskConfig.ToConfig() to rebuild a usable config.Config from the curated payload. Added storage.WorktreeMountDir constant (/data/worktree) — critical fix: hybridTrees.Prepare discards the RPC response's host-side directory and returns the container's fixed local mount path instead, since archied and archie-agent see the same files at different paths. Wired a queue-grouped core-NATS subscription on archie.taskrun.> in cmd/archie-agent/main.go so this is reachable in the running binary, not just testable in isolation. End-to-end test drives the real 'bootstrap' workflow (no LLM) through real storerpc/forgerpc/worktreerpc servers and a real local git remote, proving the full chain: registry build, route, prepare, commit, push, PR creation, and that the authoritative task state lands in archied's store via RPC. archie-core-5zh.8 (daemon.go handoff) is now unblocked — it owns deciding exactly how/when archied publishes to archie.taskrun.<id>.

daemon.process() now branches on d.ContainerPool != nil: sandboxed tasks get handed to archie-agent via a new runViaAgent method (publishes taskrun.Request to archie.taskrun.<id>, awaits taskrun.Response) instead of calling workflow.Route/workflow.Run locally; non-container mode is unchanged. runViaAgent only parks the task itself on transport/setup failure (encode error, no responder, decode error, or an error returned before archie-agent's workflow.Run got to run) — on success, every durable side effect already landed via the storerpc/forgerpc/worktreerpc proxies during archie-agent's run, so runViaAgent just logs. Added agentexec.ProvidersFromConfig (deduped from cmd/archied's former executionProviders). Also fixed a real correctness gap this surfaced: with concurrent multi-task dispatch (u64/g1l) plus containerized archie-agent, the 5zh.7 wildcard queue-group subscription could let one container answer a sibling's taskrun message despite having a different task's worktree mounted. archie-agent now reads its boot-time task.json (container.TaskPayload, already written by daemon.process() before container acquire) and subscribes to its own exact archie.taskrun.<id> subject when present, falling back to the shared queue group only when no task.json exists (dev/pool mode). Full container-mode integration (real Docker) isn't covered by an automated test, consistent with the rest of the container-dependent code — runViaAgent itself is unit-tested directly against embedded NATS, bypassing the Docker-dependent Acquire path. This closes the archie-core-5zh epic: archie-agent now runs an entire task's workflow per invocation instead of one stage per round trip, with Store/Forge/git-push credentials staying daemon-side throughout.

All sub-issues (5zh.1 Store RPC, 5zh.2 Forge RPC, 5zh.3 worktree Prepare/Push RPC, 5zh.5 curated TaskConfig payload, 5zh.6 TaskContext interface refactor, 5zh.7 archie-agent full-task handler, 5zh.9 register RPC servers, 5zh.8 daemon handoff) are closed. Original acceptance criterion met: workflow.Route and workflow.Run execute inside archie-agent, not archied, in sandboxed NATS+container mode; archie-agent handles a full task per invocation. inprocess/subprocess modes unaffected.

Persistent container/worktree storage now has configured TTL expiry. Repos opting into persistent_storage retain an Archie-owned Docker repo volume and reuse a per-repo bare Git object cache to avoid repeated full network clones while keeping issue worktrees isolated via dissociated clones. containers.volume_ttl defaults to 72h; daemon startup/cycles automatically remove expired owned repo volumes and Git caches. Tests cover config default/validation, Docker ownership labels and selective expiry, cache reuse/isolation/expiry/path safety, and daemon TTL wiring. Full race suite, vet, build, formatting, and scoped staticcheck pass.

Implemented config.LoadOverlay (base decode + overlay decode into same struct, then shared finalize/validate), wired -config-overlay flag in cmd/archied, fixed docker-compose.yml to mount both base config.toml and config.docker.toml overlay, minimized config.docker.toml to true diff-only overlay, added tests proving overlay-omitted required fields (bot_user, repos) still come from base.
